Item 1. Business

Acme designs accelerated computing platforms for data centers, gaming and automotive markets.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

In addition to the other information set forth in this report, you should carefully consider the factors discussed below, which could materially affect our business, financial condition or future results.

Failure to meet the evolving needs of our industry may adversely impact our financial results.

Our accelerated computing platforms face intense competition from established semiconductor companies and from our own customers who develop internal solutions. If we are unable to anticipate customer demand and deliver competitive products on time, our revenue and margins could decline materially.

Adverse economic conditions may harm our business.

Economic uncertainty, inflation, higher interest rates and tariff changes may cause customers to delay or reduce purchases. A decline in end-market demand could result in excess inventory, impairment charges and lower gross margin.

Changes in export controls and trade regulations could negatively impact our business.

The U.S. government has imposed and may further impose export restrictions on our products sold to China and other regions. Such regulations could require licenses we cannot obtain, reduce our addressable market, and increase litigation and compliance costs.

We depend on a limited number of third-party foundries and suppliers for manufacturing.

Supply constraints, capacity shortages or disruptions at our foundry and packaging partners could limit our ability to meet demand, delay product transitions and increase our costs, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

Our stock price may be volatile and may decline regardless of our operating performance.

The market price of our common stock has fluctuated significantly and could continue to fluctuate in response to quarterly results, guidance, announcements by competitors or customers, changes in analyst estimates, and broader market and macroeconomic conditions, including tariff and interest rate uncertainty.

We are subject to litigation and regulatory investigations that could be costly and divert management attention.

From time to time we are involved in legal proceedings, including securities class actions, antitrust investigations and intellectual property claims. An unfavorable outcome could require us to pay substantial damages, change our business practices, or restrict sales of certain products, which could adversely affect our results.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

The following discussion should be read in conjunction with the condensed consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included elsewhere in this report and the audited financial statements in our annual report.

Revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 was $12.3 billion, up 23% from a year ago, driven by strong demand for data center accelerators and networking products. We expect demand to continue to exceed supply for several quarters as customers accelerate capacity build-outs.

Gross margin was 61.2%, compared with 58.9% a year ago, reflecting a favorable product mix partially offset by higher inventory provisions and tariff costs on certain components. We anticipate gross margin in the low 60s for the remainder of the fiscal year, subject to pricing and supply constraints.

Operating expenses increased 18% year over year, primarily due to compensation and benefits, including stock-based compensation, reflecting headcount growth and higher engineering development costs. We expect operating expense growth to moderate in the second half.

Export controls adopted by the U.S. government continue to restrict sales of certain products to customers in China. These regulations have reduced our revenue from China and may continue to create uncertainty in demand and pricing in that region.

Liquidity remains strong. As of the end of the quarter we had $48.1 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. During the quarter we repurchased $6.0 billion of common stock and paid $0.2 billion in dividends. Capital expenditures were $1.1 billion.

Outlook: revenue for the third quarter is expected to be $13.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. Gross margin is expected to be 61.5%, plus or minus 50 basis points, and operating expenses are expected to grow in the mid-teens percent sequentially.
